t.r: Turkish Aegean and Mediterranean coast (Bodrum, Marmaris)
t.p: traditional; Bodrum type from the early 1970s
t.d: Wooden two- or three-masted gulets built for the Blue Cruise, popularised by Cevat Şakir Kabaağaçlı.
t.auth: Bodrum or Marmaris build; clipper stem with rounded stern or transom stern; sailing rig fitted rather than motor-only

t.d: Seaworthy double-ended pilot and rescue boats by Colin Archer, later copied as cruising yachts.
t.auth: original Archer build records and RS numbers versus later replicas

t.d: Aleut skin-on-frame kayak with forked bow, lashed driftwood frame and sea-lion skin sewn by women.

t.r: Eastern Canada and north-eastern United States
t.d: Indigenous craft of building canoes from paper-birch bark over a cedar frame, later adopted for the fur trade.
t.tech: bark sewn with split roots over cedar ribs and planking; seams sealed with resin
t.mat: paper birch bark, cedar, spruce root, resin

t.d: Specialised trade building horse-drawn coach and carriage bodies and undercarriages.
t.tech: Cabinet-style joinery of curved timber framing; separate body-maker, carriage-maker, coach-smith, trimmer and painter
t.mat: Ash, beech, elm, oak, mahogany; iron axles and springs; leather; brass
ctr: Worshipful Company of Coachmakers and Coach Harness Makers (1630)
t.auth: Builder's plates and maker records; period joinery, springs and trimming

t.d: Inuit skin-on-frame hunting kayak and its rolling skills, kept alive by the Greenland Kayaking Championships with 35 rolls and manoeuvres.
t.tech: skin-on-frame hull sized to the paddler; rolling
t.mat: wood frame, sealskin or fabric skin

t.d: Building and decorating vardo living wagons with carving, scrollwork and gold leaf.
t.tech: Tongue-and-groove panelling, carved ornament, painted scrollwork, gilding
t.mat: Timber, canvas (bow top), cast-iron stove, gold leaf
t.auth: Wagon type by body shape and wheel placement; carving and painting by known wagon artists

t.d: Craft of building and repairing wooden spoked wheels for carts, wagons and carriages.
t.tech: Nave, spokes and felloes built from the centre out; spokes tenoned into the nave; hot iron tyre shrunk on; dishing and staggered spokes
t.mat: Elm nave, oak spokes, ash felloes (hickory, black locust); iron or steel tyre
t.auth: Wooden nave, spokes and felloes with a shrunk-on tyre; dish and spoke stagger
